key_insight: Euclidean fast attention is a linear-scaling attention mechanism that uses Euclidean rotary encodings to encode 3D positions, enabling scalable, rotation-aware global atomic representations that accurately capture long-range interactions in physical systems.
problem_solved: Standard attention has quadratic compute and memory cost and struggles to scale to large 3D atomic systems and long-range physical effects; this work removes that bottleneck while preserving Euclidean (rotation/translation) structure.
method: Introduce Euclidean rotary encodings to represent 3D coordinates in a rotation-aware manner inside attention.
Reformulate attention into a linear (fast) attention kernel that reduces compute/memory from O(N^2) to O(N) for atoms/points.
Integrate the fast Euclidean attention into global atomic representation models to capture long-range interactions efficiently.
impact: Makes transformer-style models practical for much larger molecular/material systems and long-range physics-aware predictions, lowering resource cost for training and inference and enabling more accurate ML potentials and simulation surrogates.

paper_title: Machine learning global atomic representations with Euclidean fast attention
paper_authors: J. Thorben Frank, Stefan Chmiela, Klaus-Robert Müller, Oliver T. Unke
